# REST reference

238 routes under `/api/v1`. Auth: `Authorization: Bearer slate_<id>_<secret>` on every call except `POST /bootstrap`. **Scope** is the least a token needs (`admin` > `write` > `read`). **ETag** routes answer `If-None-Match` with a body-less `304`. **MCP** names the tool action that makes the same call. `*` marks a required body field. Conventions (errors, paging, cursors, rate limits) are in [../rest.md](../rest.md); the live schema is `/openapi.json` and `/docs` on a running Slate.

## accounts

### `POST /bootstrap`

Scope: `none`

First run only (no accounts yet): create the first person with an admin token.

- Body: `BootstrapIn`: `handle`\*, `display_name`\*
- Returns: `201` [BootstrapOut](#bootstrapout)

### `GET /me`

Scope: `read` · ETag · MCP: `slate_account me`

Who this token is, its scopes, board prefs and `access`: the role's reach through this token (every list, or the sections/lists it can see with their level). The board hides what `access` rules out; the server enforces it regardless. A browser session also gets its cookie's lifetime renewed here (`session_expires_at` says when the session itself ends).

- Returns: `200` [MeOut](#meout)

### `PATCH /me/prefs`

Scope: `write`

Merge into your board prefs (a key sent as null is removed) and return them all. The change reaches your other devices live as `account.prefs_changed`.

- Body: `Prefs`: `theme`, `collapsed`, `last_view`, `email_to`, `email_reasons`, `view_drafts`
- Returns: `200`

### `GET /accounts`

Scope: `admin` · ETag · MCP: `slate_account list`

List Accounts

- Returns: `200` [list of AccountOut](#accountout)

### `POST /accounts`

Scope: `admin` · MCP: `slate_account create`

Create a person or agent. `role` defaults to member; a guest sees only what is shared with it; only the owner creates admins.

- Body: `AccountIn`: `handle`\*, `display_name`\*, `kind`\*, `role`, `wake`
- Returns: `201` [AccountOut](#accountout)

### `PATCH /accounts/{account_id}`

Scope: `admin` · MCP: `slate_account update`

Rename an account, or disable it (`disabled: true`): its tokens stop working at once, it leaves the roster, its history and assignments stay. `disabled: false` re-enables it. You cannot disable yourself. `wake` sets how an agent is woken: `push` (a runner), `pull` (its own product polls; Run now nudges its owner) or `manual` (Copy brief). The `slate` account is Slate's own (due dates, reminders and automations are recorded as it, source `system`) and cannot be changed: 422.

- Body: `AccountPatch`: `display_name`, `disabled`, `wake`
- Returns: `200` [AccountOut](#accountout)

### `GET /accounts/{account_id}/tokens`

Scope: `read` · MCP: `slate_account tokens`

An account's tokens, newest first, with `last_used_at` (never the secret). Admins can list anyone's; any account can list its own.

- Query: `include_revoked`
- Returns: `200` [list of TokenOut](#tokenout)

### `GET /accounts/{account_id}/usage`

Scope: `read` · MCP: `slate_account usage`

What an account has been doing: events per day by source (`ui`, `api`, `mcp`, `system`), its busiest event types, and each live token's last use and request counts. Request counts and `throttled` are since the server last started. Admin, or yourself.

- Query: `days`
- Returns: `200` [UsageOut](#usageout)

### `POST /accounts/{account_id}/tokens`

Scope: `admin` · MCP: `slate_account create_token`

Issue a token for an account. The plaintext is in this response and nowhere else. `limit` narrows it to some sections/lists and a level (an agent that may only touch one list); a token never reaches further than its account's role and shares.

- Body: `TokenIn`: `scopes`\*, `label`, `limit`
- Returns: `201` [TokenCreatedOut](#tokencreatedout)

### `DELETE /tokens/{token_id}`

Scope: `read` · MCP: `slate_account revoke_token`

Revoke a token. Admins can revoke any token; any account can revoke its own.

- Returns: `204`

## agent connections

### `POST /agent-connections/pairings`

Scope: `admin`

Create explicit list-scoped consent; return the expiring single-use code once.

- Body: `PairingIn`: `account_id`\*, `label`\*, `list_ids`\*, `ttl_seconds`
- Returns: `201`

### `POST /agent-connections/exchange`

Scope: `none`

Exchange one code for one scoped credential. Validation never echoes secret input.

- Returns: `200`

### `GET /agent-connections`

Scope: `read`

Private connection lifecycle for self or unrestricted account managers only.

- Query: `account_id`\*
- Returns: `200`

### `POST /agent-connections/{connection_id}/heartbeat`

Scope: `write`

Exact connection credential reports a canned health check, not arbitrary diagnostics.

- Body: `slate__api__connections__HeartbeatIn`: `check`\*, `capabilities`
- Returns: `200`

### `DELETE /agent-connections/{connection_id}`

Scope: `read`

Disconnect one credential without claiming a remote process has stopped.

- Returns: `204`

## collaboration

### `POST /invitations`

Scope: `admin`

Invite a guest person to edit one active private section; secret returned only once.

- Body: `InviteIn`: `section_id`\*, `handle`\*, `display_name`\*, `role`, `level`
- Returns: `201`

### `GET /invitations`

Scope: `admin`

Invitation lifecycle for a section (admin only), never credentials or hashes. Each row carries `session_expires_at` / `session_revoked_at` of the browser session it issued.

- Query: `section_id`\*
- Returns: `200`

### `POST /invitations/{invitation_id}/extend`

Scope: `admin`

Push the accepted invitation's browser session out to thirty days from now (`session.extended`). 422 before acceptance; 410 once cancelled or signed out.

- Returns: `200`

### `POST /invitations/{invitation_id}/reissue`

Scope: `admin`

A fresh single-use link for the same guest and section, for another device or a link opened in the wrong app; the original stays valid. Secret returned only once.

- Returns: `201`

### `DELETE /invitations/{invitation_id}`

Scope: `admin`

Cancel an invitation and its issued session; remove shares separately to end all access.

- Returns: `204`

### `POST /invitations/accept`

Scope: `none`

Consume a single-use link; sign in this browser for thirty days. Not email verification.

- Body: `AcceptIn`: `secret`\*
- Returns: `200`

### `POST /session/logout`

Scope: `read`

Revoke the current credential and remove this browser's session cookie.

- Returns: `204`

### `GET /sections/{section_id}/project`

Scope: `read`

Section project home metadata and scoped participant identities (no workspace presence).

- Returns: `200`

## permissions

### `GET /members`

Scope: `admin`

Every account (people and agents) with its role, how many shares it holds and when it last did anything. The Members page.

- Returns: `200` [list of MemberOut](#memberout)

### `PUT /accounts/{account_id}/role`

Scope: `admin` · MCP: `slate_account set_role`

Change an account's role. Members see everything not private; guests only what is shared with them. Only the owner makes or unmakes admins; `owner` hands ownership over.

- Body: `RoleIn`: `role`\*
- Returns: `200` [AccountOut](#accountout)

### `GET /accounts/{account_id}/access`

Scope: `read` · MCP: `slate_account access`

What an account reaches with an unlimited token: every section and list with its level. Admin, or yourself.

- Returns: `200` [AccountAccessOut](#accountaccessout)

### `GET /shares`

Scope: `admin` · MCP: `slate_share list`

List Shares

- Query: `account_id`, `scope_kind`, `scope_id`
- Returns: `200` [list of ShareOut](#shareout)

### `PUT /shares`

Scope: `admin` · MCP: `slate_share set`

Share a section or list with an account at `view`, `comment` or `edit` (or change the level; `level: null` revokes). Returns the share, or null when revoked.

- Body: `ShareIn`: `account_id`\*, `scope_kind`\*, `scope_id`\*, `level`\*
- Returns: `200`

### `DELETE /shares/{share_id}`

Scope: `admin`

Delete Share

- Returns: `204`

### `GET /sections/{section_id}/access`

Scope: `admin`

Everyone who reaches this section, at what level and why (the sharing dialog).

- Returns: `200` [list of AccessRow](#accessrow)

### `GET /lists/{list_id}/access`

Scope: `admin` · MCP: `slate_share who`

Everyone who reaches this list, at what level and why (the sharing dialog).

- Returns: `200` [list of AccessRow](#accessrow)

### `GET /audit`

Scope: `read` · MCP: `slate_audit list`

Who (person or agent) did what, when and through which door, newest first. Read-only. Owners and admins see everything; anyone else sees the lists they can read and their own actions.

- Query: `actor`, `actor_kind`, `source`, `type`, `item_id`, `list_id`, `section_id`, `since`, `until`, `q`, `before`, `limit`
- Returns: `200` [AuditPage](#auditpage)

### `GET /audit/facets`

Scope: `read` · MCP: `slate_audit facets`

Event types and actors that appear in the log you can see, for filter menus.

- Returns: `200` [AuditFacets](#auditfacets)

### `GET /audit.csv`

Scope: `read`

The audit log with the same filters, as CSV (newest first, up to 50,000 rows).

- Query: `actor`, `actor_kind`, `source`, `type`, `item_id`, `list_id`, `section_id`, `since`, `until`, `q`
- Returns: `200`

- Returns: `200` [list of SectionOut](#sectionout)

### `PATCH /sections/{section_id}`

## lists

### `GET /lists`

Scope: `read` · ETag · MCP: `slate_list list`

List Lists

- Query: `section_id`, `include_archived`
- Returns: `200` [list of ListOut](#listout)

### `GET /lists/{list_id}`

Scope: `read` · ETag

Get List

- Returns: `200` [ListOut](#listout)

### `POST /lists`

Scope: `write` · MCP: `slate_list create`

Create a list in a section. Without `statuses` it gets To do -> In progress -> Done.

- Body: `ListIn`: `section_id`\*, `name`\*, `position`, `statuses`, `kind`
- Returns: `201` [ListOut](#listout)

### `PATCH /lists/{list_id}`

Scope: `write` · MCP: `slate_list update`, `slate_share private`

Rename, reorder, move to another section, set the default status, archive (`archived: true`) / restore, or make it private (owner/admin; `private: true`).

- Body: `ListPatch`: `name`, `kind`, `section_id`, `position`, `default_status`, `archived`, `private`
- Returns: `200` [ListOut](#listout)

### `PUT /lists/{list_id}/statuses`

Scope: `write` · MCP: `slate_list set_statuses`

Replace the list's statuses, in order, in one change.

- Body: `StatusesPut`: `statuses`\*, `fallback`
- Returns: `200` [ListOut](#listout)

## items

### `GET /items`

Scope: `read` · ETag · MCP: `slate_item list`

Filters combine with AND. `status` is an id or name; `assignee` a handle; `tag` a name; due bounds are exclusive and accept ISO 8601 or YYYY-MM-DD; `q` matches title or body; `stale` = due date moved 3+ times, or open and untouched for 30+ days; `blocked` = waits on an open item (true) or on none (false).

- Query: `list_id`, `section_id`, `status`, `assignee`, `tag`, `external_ref`, `due_before`, `due_after`, `q`, `stale`, `include_archived`, `archived`, `trashed`, `closed`, `order`, `kind`, `blocked`, `changed_since`, `fields`, `limit`, `offset`, `ids`, `open_comment_for`
- Returns: `200` [list of ItemOut](#itemout)

### `POST /items`

Scope: `write` · MCP: `slate_item create`

Create exactly one item; never children. `parent_id` makes it a subtask; subtasks nest four deep under a top task. Use `POST /items/{id}/split` to create several subtasks.

- Body: `ItemIn`: `body_md`, `body_note`, `status`, `priority`, `start_at`, `due_at`, `waiting_on_account_id`, `acceptance_md`, `position`, `kind`, `external_ref`, `assignees`, `tags`, `estimate_minutes`, `title`\*, `list_id`, `parent_id`
- Returns: `201` [ItemOut](#itemout)

### `POST /items/ai`

Scope: `write`

AI add: file exactly one item from plain words (title = the first sentence, description = all of it, plus `defaults`) and return it at once; then the configured Ollama model (`SLATE_AI_URL`, `SLATE_AI_MODEL`) fills in the title, description, assignees, dates, priority, status and tags the words decide, written as Slate's own account (`session_ref` `ai-add`) and seen through the stream. Fields changed before the model answers are left alone. 409 when AI add is off (`GET /me` `ai_add`).

- Body: `AiItemIn`: `list_id`\*, `text`\*, `defaults`
- Returns: `201` [ItemOut](#itemout)

### `GET /items/{item_id}`

Scope: `read` · ETag · MCP: `slate_item get`

The item with its subtasks, tags, assignees, comments and last 20 events.

- Returns: `200` [ItemDetailOut](#itemdetailout)

### `PATCH /items/{item_id}`

Scope: `write` · MCP: `slate_item update`, `slate_item set_status`, `slate_item assign`, `slate_item tag`

Send only what changes; `null` clears a field. `status` by id or name; `assignees` (handles) and `tags` (names) replace the whole set.

- Body: `ItemPatch`: `body_md`, `body_note`, `status`, `priority`, `start_at`, `due_at`, `waiting_on_account_id`, `acceptance_md`, `position`, `kind`, `external_ref`, `assignees`, `tags`, `estimate_minutes`, `title`
- Returns: `200` [ItemOut](#itemout)

### `POST /items/bulk`

Scope: `write` · MCP: `slate_item bulk_update`

One change applied to many items: every PATCH field, plus add_tags, remove_tags, archive, trash (true/false, sent alone: to the trash and back), list_id (move to another list; subtasks follow their parent) and status_kind (each item gets its own list's first status of that kind, so one call works across lists). All or nothing; one event per item per changed field.

- Body: `BulkIn`: `ids`\*, `changes`\*
- Returns: `200` [list of ItemOut](#itemout)

### `DELETE /items/{item_id}`

Scope: `write` · MCP: `slate_item delete`

Undo a create: only its creator, only within 10 minutes. Otherwise archive it.

- Returns: `204`

### `POST /items/{item_id}/archive`

Scope: `write` · MCP: `slate_item archive`

Hide the item (and its subtasks). History, comments and versions stay.

- Returns: `200` [ItemOut](#itemout)

### `POST /items/{item_id}/unarchive`

Scope: `write` · MCP: `slate_item unarchive`

Unarchive Item

- Returns: `200` [ItemOut](#itemout)

### `POST /items/{item_id}/trash`

Scope: `write` · MCP: `slate_item trash`

Move the item (and its subtasks) to the trash: hidden everywhere, restorable, deleted for good after the trash period (30 days by default).

- Returns: `200` [ItemOut](#itemout)

### `POST /items/{item_id}/restore`

Scope: `write` · MCP: `slate_item restore`

Take the item (and the subtasks trashed with it) out of the trash.

- Returns: `200` [ItemOut](#itemout)

### `POST /items/{item_id}/purge`

Scope: `write` · MCP: `slate_item purge`

Delete a trashed item for good, with its subtasks. Its history stays.

- Returns: `204`

### `POST /items/{item_id}/split`

Scope: `write` · MCP: `slate_item split`

The only way to create several subtasks at once.

- Body: `SplitIn`: `children`\*
- Returns: `201` [list of ItemOut](#itemout)

### `GET /items/{item_id}/events`

Scope: `read` · ETag · MCP: `slate_item history`

The item's full history, oldest first.

- Returns: `200` [list of slate__api__schemas__EventOut](#slate__api__schemas__eventout)

### `GET /items/{item_id}/versions`

Scope: `read` · ETag · MCP: `slate_item versions`

Every body version, oldest first.

- Returns: `200` [list of slate__api__schemas__VersionOut](#slate__api__schemas__versionout)

### `GET /items/{item_id}/activity`

Scope: `read` · ETag · MCP: `slate_item activity`

Comments and history in one list, oldest first: what the task window's right column shows. `limit` keeps the newest entries.

- Query: `include`, `limit`
- Returns: `200` [list of ActivityOut](#activityout)

### `GET /items/{item_id}/watchers`

Scope: `read` · ETag · MCP: `slate_item watchers`

List Watchers

- Returns: `200` [list of AssigneeOut](#assigneeout)

### `PUT /items/{item_id}/watchers`

Scope: `write` · MCP: `slate_item set_watchers`

Replace who watches the item.

- Body: `WatchersIn`: `watchers`\*
- Returns: `200` [list of AssigneeOut](#assigneeout)

### `POST /items/{item_id}/watch`

Scope: `write` · MCP: `slate_item watch`

Add a watcher: yourself, or `account` (a person or agent; they are told you added them). A watcher hears about every change to the item (inbox `watching`, check-in `watching`, an `assignee_me` webhook).

- Body: JSON (see `/openapi.json`)
- Returns: `200` [list of AssigneeOut](#assigneeout)

### `POST /items/{item_id}/unwatch`

Scope: `write` · MCP: `slate_item unwatch`

Remove a watcher: yourself, or `account`.

- Body: JSON (see `/openapi.json`)
- Returns: `200` [list of AssigneeOut](#assigneeout)

### `POST /items/{item_id}/report`

Scope: `write` · MCP: `slate_item report`

An agent says what it is doing: `working`, `blocked` or `review` put a live badge on the card (who, note, progress); `done` clears it and completes the item (unless `complete: false`); `idle` just clears it. The note is also posted as your comment. `blocked` + `waiting_on: alex` puts the item in that person's Today "waiting on me".

- Body: `ReportIn`: `run_id`, `state`\*, `note`, `progress`, `comment`, `complete`, `waiting_on`, `assign_me`, `url`, `claim`, `reply`, `thread`
- Returns: `200` [ItemOut](#itemout)

### `POST /items/{item_id}/run`

Scope: `write` · MCP: `slate_item run`

Run now: ask the item's agent assignees to start on it now instead of at its run time. Records `item.run_requested` (`after.for` = the agents), which reaches each agent's stream as a `work` hint (its runner then takes this task with `POST /work/next {item_id}`) and webhooks. 422 when no agent is assigned or the item is done, cancelled or archived.

- Returns: `202` [slate__api__schemas__EventOut](#slate__api__schemas__eventout)

### `GET /items/{item_id}/brief`

Scope: `read` · MCP: `slate_item brief`

The task as one paste-ready prompt for an agent in another product's chat ("Copy brief"): title, due date, description, checklists and recent comments, then the run rule, which asks it to end its answer with `SLATE: done`, `SLATE: review`, `SLATE: later` (the rest waits for the due time) or `SLATE: blocked waiting_on <ask>`. Post that answer back as a comment and the line reports on the task. `ask` (a handle) defaults to you, or the workspace owner.

- Query: `ask`
- Returns: `200` [BriefOut](#briefout)

## comments

### `GET /items/{item_id}/comments`

Scope: `read` · ETag · MCP: `slate_comment list`

The item's comments, oldest first, with reactions and mentions.

- Returns: `200` [list of CommentOut](#commentout)

### `POST /items/{item_id}/comments`

Scope: `write` · MCP: `slate_item comment`, `slate_comment add`

`@handle` in the body mentions that account (see webhooks: `assignee_me` hears it). `assignee` makes it an Ask: addressed to that account, open until explicitly resolved. Replies notify earlier participants but never resolve Asks; `keep_open` is accepted for compatibility. A last line `SLATE: done`, `SLATE: review`, `SLATE: later` or `SLATE: blocked waiting_on <handle>` also reports back on the task (from an agent: its report, later clearing its badge until the due time; from a person, done completes it and blocked sets who it waits on).

- Body: `CommentIn`: `body_md`\*, `assignee`, `keep_open`
- Returns: `201` [CommentOut](#commentout)

### `PATCH /comments/{comment_id}`

Scope: `write` · MCP: `slate_comment assign`, `slate_comment edit`

Edit your own comment's text (403 for anyone else's), and/or address it to someone (`assignee`, null to take it off; the author or an admin).

- Body: `CommentPatch`: `body_md`, `assignee`
- Returns: `200` [CommentOut](#commentout)

### `DELETE /comments/{comment_id}`

Scope: `write` · MCP: `slate_comment delete`

Delete a comment for good: your own, or anyone's if you are an owner or admin (403 otherwise). Its reactions go too; the `comment.deleted` event keeps what it said.

- Returns: `204`

### `POST /comments/{comment_id}/resolve`

Scope: `write` · MCP: `slate_comment resolve`

Close an Ask: for its assignee, its author or an admin. Idempotent.

- Returns: `200` [CommentOut](#commentout)

### `POST /comments/{comment_id}/reactions`

Scope: `write` · MCP: `slate_comment react`

Add your emoji reaction (idempotent).

- Body: `ReactionIn`: `emoji`\*
- Returns: `200` [CommentOut](#commentout)

### `DELETE /comments/{comment_id}/reactions/{emoji}`

Scope: `write` · MCP: `slate_comment unreact`

Take back your emoji reaction (idempotent).

- Returns: `200` [CommentOut](#commentout)

### `POST /items/{item_id}/read`

Scope: `write`

You opened the item: its comments so far are no longer new to you, so its card's comment dot clears. `read_at` is null when nothing was new (nothing is written).

- Returns: `200` [ItemReadOut](#itemreadout)

### `GET /me/comment-dots`

Scope: `read`

Item id -> the comment dot its card shows you, for every item with comments new to you since you last opened it: `mention` (you are @mentioned or asked, by anyone), `human` (a person commented) or `agent` (only agents did). Your own comments never count.

- Returns: `200`

## attachments

### `GET /items/{item_id}/attachments`

Scope: `read` · ETag · MCP: `slate_item attachments`

List Attachments

- Returns: `200` [list of AttachmentOut](#attachmentout)

### `POST /items/{item_id}/attachments`

Scope: `write`

Attach a file (raw body, up to 25 MB).

- Query: `filename`\*
- Body: `application/octet-stream`
- Returns: `201` [AttachmentOut](#attachmentout)

### `POST /items/{item_id}/attachments/base64`

Scope: `write` · MCP: `slate_item attach`

The same as the raw upload, for clients that can only send JSON (the MCP stdio bridge).

## stats

### `GET /stats`

Scope: `read`

Request latency per route (time to first byte, last 1,000 requests of each route, since the process started), plus counts. Every API response also carries `Server-Timing`. `write_lock`: how long the last 2,000 changes waited for the single writer and held it. `item_cache`: whole-item JSON kept for `GET /items` and `/today`. Owners and admins, like `/health`: it names the database file and counts every account.

- Returns: `200` [StatsOut](#statsout)

## batch

### `POST /batch`

Scope: `read` · MCP: `slate_batch run`

Up to 100 operations in one round trip. Each op is an MCP call: `{tool, action, params, ref?}` (tool `item`, `comment`, `list`...; see docs/agents/reference/mcp.md); a string param `$ref.field` uses an earlier op's result. `atomic` (default) commits all or nothing: on a failure the answer is that op's error status with `failed_op` (its index) and nothing is written. `atomic: false` runs each op on its own and reports each slot. Each op needs its own scope (a read token can batch reads).

- Body: `BatchIn`: `ops`\*, `atomic`, `views`
- Returns: `200` [BatchOut](#batchout)

## agents

### `GET /agents/plan`

Scope: `read` · MCP: `slate_work plan`

What each agent is about to run in the next 24 hours, read with the work loop's own rule (`POST /work/next`): tasks whose run time comes (the due gate), tasks someone pressed Run now on, open Asks addressed to it, and the tasks it holds now with their age. Agents with the soonest work first. A restricted token sees only the agents and lists it reaches.

- Returns: `200` [PlanOut](#planout)

### `GET /agents`

Scope: `read` · MCP: `slate_agents list`

Who is around and what each is on: `online` (a request in the last 2 minutes or an open live stream), `last_seen_at`, `working` (items with that account's current report), `open_assigned`, `events_24h`, `throttled` (requests refused by the rate limit since the process started) and `wake` (how a task reaches it: push, pull or manual). Agents by default; `kind=person` or `all`.

- Query: `kind`
- Returns: `200` [list of AgentOut](#agentout)

## checkin

### `GET /checkin`

Scope: `read` · ETag · MCP: `slate_checkin get`

What to work on and what changed for you, in one call. `queue`: your open items (assigned or waiting on you). `news`: other accounts' events that concern you, each with `why` (assigned, unassigned, mentioned, reply, waiting_on_you, on_your_item, watching, reminder, digest); a chat mention or thread reply carries the message in `after`. Keep `next_since` and pass it as `since` next time; without `since` you get the latest news. The queue is the most urgent `queue_limit` (50) of `queue_total`; `fields=id,title,due_at` keeps it small. With `since` and `wait`, an empty answer waits (long-poll) until news arrives or `wait` seconds pass; `/checkin/stream` is the same news pushed live.

- Query: `since`, `limit`, `queue_limit`, `fields`, `wait`
- Returns: `200` [CheckinOut](#checkinout)

### `GET /checkin/stream`

Scope: `read`

Your check-in, pushed live: react instead of polling. Two SSE event names, both with `id` = the event id (your resume cursor; EventSource resends it as `Last-Event-ID`): `news` = an event that concerns you (the `/checkin` news shape, with `why`); `work` = a task you could take with `POST /work/next` just became free (`{id, item_id, type}`: it was assigned to you, unblocked, released...), or a chat mention to answer (`{id, type: message.mentioned_agent, channel, thread_id, message_id, queued}`: take it with `POST /work/next {channel, thread_id}`; `queued` means your open turn there takes it, no new run), or a doc mention (`{id, type: doc.mentioned_agent, doc_id, thread_id, comment_id, queued}`: take it with `POST /work/next {doc_id, thread_id}`). With `since` or `Last-Event-ID` it first replays what you missed; a `: ready` comment marks the switch to live. Token in the `Authorization` header (or `?token=`); you only hear about lists you can see.

- Query: `since`, `pool`, `token`
- Returns: `200`

## work

### `POST /work/next`

Scope: `write` · MCP: `slate_work next`

Take your next task in one call: the best open task assigned to you or waiting on you (with `pool`, also unassigned ones) that is not blocked by an open task, not started later, not held by another agent and not waiting on a person. Order: priority, due date, board position. An agent's assigned task with a due date waits for its run time (06:00 workspace time on the day for a date-only due date, else the due time) unless someone pressed Run now. `item_id` takes that task or nothing. It is yours (live 'working' badge, assigned) for `lease_seconds`; heartbeat to keep it, finish to report back. With `wait`, holds the request up to that many seconds until a task frees up. `item` is null when none is free.

- Body: `NextIn`: `kinds`, `run_id`, `lease_seconds`, `pool`, `list_id`, `section_id`, `tag`, `item_id`, `channel`, `thread_id`, `doc_id`, `resume`, `note`, `context`, `wait`
- Returns: `200` [NextOut](#nextout)

### `GET /work`

Scope: `read` · MCP: `slate_work held`

The tasks you hold now, soonest lease to run out first.

- Returns: `200` [list of LeaseOut](#leaseout)

### `POST /work/chat/reconcile`

Scope: `write` · MCP: `slate_work chat_reconcile`

Confirm remote termination with retained run proof; local process exit is not evidence.

- Body: `ChatReconcileIn`: `run_id`\*, `state`\*, `evidence`\*, `channel`\*, `thread_id`
- Returns: `200`

### `POST /work/doc/reconcile`

Scope: `write` · MCP: `slate_work doc_reconcile`

Confirm remote termination of a doc turn with retained run proof (after it expired).

- Body: `DocReconcileIn`: `run_id`\*, `state`\*, `evidence`\*, `doc_id`\*, `thread_id`
- Returns: `200`

### `POST /work/chat/clear`

Scope: `write` · MCP: `slate_work chat_clear`

Clear an agent's expired chat turn (the board's "stopped answering" line): a person who may post in the channel confirms the run is over, because its runner lost the proof it needs to reconcile. Records `message.agent_turn` `state: released`, `reconciled`, with you as the actor; a mention that waited in the turn is the agent's next turn. 403 for an agent (it reconciles its own turn with its run proof); 409 when there is no expired turn there (a live turn ends when the agent finishes or its lease runs out).

- Body: `ChatClearIn`: `channel`\*, `thread_id`, `agent_id`\*
- Returns: `200` [ClearOut](#clearout)

### `POST /work/doc/clear`

Scope: `write` · MCP: `slate_work doc_clear`

Clear an agent's expired doc turn, the same contract as `/work/chat/clear`: a person who may comment on the doc confirms the run is over (`doc.agent_turn` `state: released`, `reconciled`, by you).

- Body: `DocClearIn`: `doc_id`\*, `thread_id`, `agent_id`\*
- Returns: `200` [ClearOut](#clearout)

### `POST /work/{item_id}/reconcile`

Scope: `write` · MCP: `slate_work reconcile`

Confirm remote termination with retained run proof; unlock without completing the task.

- Body: `ReconcileIn`: `run_id`\*, `state`\*, `evidence`\*
- Returns: `200`

### `POST /work/chat/heartbeat`

Scope: `write` · MCP: `slate_work chat_heartbeat`

Keep holding a chat turn (`chat` from `/work/next`): the lease runs `lease_seconds` from now. 409 when you hold no open turn there (it ended or ran out).

- Body: `ChatHeartbeatIn`: `run_id`, `channel`\*, `thread_id`, `lease_seconds`
- Returns: `200` [ChatLeaseOut](#chatleaseout)

### `POST /work/chat/finish`

Scope: `write` · MCP: `slate_work chat_finish`

End a chat turn. `done` with `reply` posts the reply as your message in the channel (in the thread when the mention was in one): that is the answer, and it reaches the board live like any message. `release` (or `done` with no reply) ends the turn with nothing posted. Any message you post in that channel or thread yourself ends the turn too, so an agent answering through `POST /channels/{key}/messages` or MCP `slate_chat post` needs no finish call. 409 when you hold no open turn there.

- Body: `ChatFinishIn`: `run_id`, `channel`\*, `thread_id`, `outcome`\*, `reply`, `note`
- Returns: `200` [ChatFinishOut](#chatfinishout)

### `POST /work/doc/heartbeat`

Scope: `write` · MCP: `slate_work doc_heartbeat`

Keep holding a doc turn (`doc` from `/work/next`): the lease runs `lease_seconds` from now. 409 when you hold no open turn there (it ended or ran out).

- Body: `DocHeartbeatIn`: `run_id`, `doc_id`\*, `thread_id`, `lease_seconds`
- Returns: `200` [ChatLeaseOut](#chatleaseout)

### `POST /work/doc/finish`

Scope: `write` · MCP: `slate_work doc_finish`

End a doc turn, the same contract as `/work/chat/finish`. `done` with `reply` posts the reply as your comment in the thread the mention was in, or as a new discussion thread on the page when the mention was in the body; it reaches the board live like any comment. `release` (or `done` with no reply) ends the turn with nothing posted. An identical retry returns the first result. 409 when you hold no open turn there.

- Body: `DocFinishIn`: `run_id`, `doc_id`\*, `thread_id`, `outcome`\*, `reply`, `note`
- Returns: `200` [DocFinishOut](#docfinishout)

### `POST /work/{item_id}/heartbeat`

Scope: `write` · MCP: `slate_work heartbeat`

Keep holding the task: the lease runs `lease_seconds` from now. `note` or `progress` also update the card's badge live. 409 means you lost it (the lease ran out and another agent took the task): stop working on it.

- Body: `slate__api__work__HeartbeatIn`: `run_id`, `lease_seconds`, `note`, `progress`, `url`, `thread`
- Returns: `200` [LeaseOut](#leaseout)

### `POST /work/{item_id}/finish`

Scope: `write` · MCP: `slate_work finish`

Report back in one round trip, all in one transaction: the outcome (done, review, later, blocked, release), a note posted as your comment, a `status`, and `hand_to` to pass the task to another account. Your lease ends. With `next`, the same call also takes your next task (and may `wait` for one). Agent finishes consume only Ask assignments present at take, so the same open Ask cannot repeatedly dispatch done, review, blocked or released work. Asks remain visible and explicitly resolvable; only asked-only agent done resolves its taken Asks (without completing the task). New or reassigned Asks during the run remain pending. Human finishes never resolve Asks.

- Body: `FinishIn`: `run_id`, `outcome`\*, `note`, `comment`, `progress`, `status`, `hand_to`, `waiting_on`, `url`, `reply`, `thread`, `next`
- Returns: `200` [FinishOut](#finishout)

Scope: `write`

Unsubscribe

Scope: `write`

Turn off this browser by its endpoint (what the board knows about itself).

### `POST /push/test`

Scope: `write`

Send a test notification to each of your devices now.

Email yourself a test notification now, to the address in your prefs (`email_to`).

## docs

### `GET /docs`

Scope: `read` · ETag · MCP: `slate_doc list`

Pages and files in tree order, without bodies. `q` searches titles, bodies, filenames and the text inside files (each hit has a `snippet`); `list_id`/`section_id` = top docs there and all under them; `workspace` = docs in no list or section; `embeds=<task or doc id>` = pages that embed or link it; `archived` = the archived docs themselves; `kind` and `tag` narrow further.

- Query: `q`, `list_id`, `section_id`, `parent_id`, `workspace`, `archived`, `embeds`, `limit`, `kind`, `tag`
- Returns: `200` [list of DocSummaryOut](#docsummaryout)

### `GET /docs/templates`

Scope: `read` · MCP: `slate_doc templates`

Starting points for a new page (`template` on create).

- Returns: `200` [list of DocTemplateOut](#doctemplateout)

### `POST /docs`

Scope: `write` · MCP: `slate_doc create`

A new page: in a list, a section, the workspace (neither), or under `parent_id`.

- Body: `DocIn`: `title`, `body_md`, `icon`, `parent_id`, `list_id`, `section_id`, `template`, `before_id`, `kind`, `tags`
- Returns: `201` [DocOut](#docout)

### `GET /docs/{doc_id}`

Scope: `read` · ETag · MCP: `slate_doc get`

The page with its body, path, subpages, outline, embedded tasks, links and files.

- Returns: `200` [DocOut](#docout)

### `PATCH /docs/{doc_id}`

Scope: `write` · MCP: `slate_doc update`

Edit title, icon or body. `append_md` and `replace_section` change part of the body; pass `base_revision` to get a 409 instead of overwriting someone else's edit.

- Body: `DocPatch`: `title`, `icon`, `body_md`, `append_md`, `replace_section`, `base_revision`, `new_version`, `note`, `tags`
- Returns: `200` [DocOut](#docout)

### `POST /docs/{doc_id}/move`

Scope: `write` · MCP: `slate_doc move`

Move a page and its subpages under another page, or to the top of a list, a section or the workspace (no parent and no place).

- Body: `DocMoveIn`: `parent_id`, `list_id`, `section_id`, `before_id`
- Returns: `200` [DocOut](#docout)

### `POST /docs/{doc_id}/archive`

Scope: `write` · MCP: `slate_doc archive`

Hide a page and its subpages.

- Returns: `200` [DocOut](#docout)

### `POST /docs/{doc_id}/unarchive`

Scope: `write` · MCP: `slate_doc unarchive`

Unarchive Doc

- Returns: `200` [DocOut](#docout)

### `DELETE /docs/{doc_id}`

Scope: `write` · MCP: `slate_doc delete`

Delete an archived page and its subpages for good (the history of events stays).

- Returns: `200` [DeletedOut](#deletedout)

### `POST /docs/{doc_id}/duplicate`

Scope: `write` · MCP: `slate_doc duplicate`

Copy a page (and its subpages) next to the original.

- Body: `DocDuplicateIn`: `title`, `subpages`
- Returns: `201` [DocOut](#docout)

### `GET /docs/{doc_id}/versions`

Scope: `read` · ETag · MCP: `slate_doc versions`

Page history, newest first, without bodies (one version per sitting of edits).

- Returns: `200` [list of slate__api__docs__VersionOut](#slate__api__docs__versionout)

### `GET /docs/{doc_id}/versions/{version_no}`

Scope: `read` · MCP: `slate_doc version`

Version

- Returns: `200` [slate__api__docs__VersionOut](#slate__api__docs__versionout)

### `POST /docs/{doc_id}/versions/{version_no}/restore`

Scope: `write` · MCP: `slate_doc restore`

Bring back an older version's title and body (as a new version).

- Returns: `200` [DocOut](#docout)

### `GET /docs/{doc_id}/diff`

Scope: `read` · MCP: `slate_doc diff`

What changed in the body between two versions (`to` default: the current text).

- Query: `from`\*, `to`
- Returns: `200` [DiffOut](#diffout)

### `POST /docs/{doc_id}/tasks`

Scope: `write` · MCP: `slate_doc create_task`

File one task from the page (create task from selection): `replace` names the text that becomes the task's live card; the task links back to the page.

- Body: `DocTaskIn`: `body_md`, `body_note`, `status`, `priority`, `start_at`, `due_at`, `waiting_on_account_id`, `acceptance_md`, `position`, `kind`, `external_ref`, `assignees`, `tags`, `estimate_minutes`, `title`\*, `list_id`, `replace`, `occurrence`, `base_revision`
- Returns: `201` [DocTaskOut](#doctaskout)

### `POST /docs/{doc_id}/files`

Scope: `write`

Upload an image or file into the page (raw body, up to 10 MB); paste its `markdown`.

- Query: `filename`\*
- Body: `application/octet-stream`
- Returns: `201` [DocFileOut](#docfileout)

### `POST /docs/{doc_id}/files/base64`

Scope: `write` · MCP: `slate_doc attach`

The same upload for clients that can only send JSON.

- Body: `Base64FileIn`: `filename`\*, `content_base64`\*, `content_type`
- Returns: `201` [DocFileOut](#docfileout)

### `GET /sections/{section_id}/documents`

Scope: `read` · MCP: `slate_doc hub`

The project home's documents hub: the section's drawers with counts, its pages outside any drawer, and what needs you (open Asks to you; open review threads by others on docs you touched).

- Returns: `200` [SectionDocumentsOut](#sectiondocumentsout)

### `GET /lists/{list_id}/drawer`

Scope: `read` · MCP: `slate_doc drawer`

A drawer's entries at its top or inside `folder`: folders and documents in tree order, each with its current and pinned revision, tags, thread counts and (for a folder) how many entries it holds; plus the folder path and the drawer's counts.

- Query: `folder`
- Returns: `200` [DrawerOut](#drawerout)

### `POST /docs/{doc_id}/to-drawer`

Scope: `write` · MCP: `slate_doc to_drawer`

Turn a top-level page into a drawer of the same name in its section: its subpages become the drawer's entries and the page itself moves in too (its text is kept).

- Returns: `201` [ListOut](#listout)

### `POST /docs/{doc_id}/revisions/{revision_no}/pin`

Scope: `write` · MCP: `slate_doc pin_revision`

Mark a revision as the one in use. One pin per document; pinning another revision moves it.

- Body: `PinIn`: `note`
- Returns: `200` [DocOut](#docout)

### `DELETE /docs/{doc_id}/pin`

Scope: `write` · MCP: `slate_doc unpin_revision`

Unpin Revision

- Returns: `200` [DocOut](#docout)

### `POST /docs/{doc_id}/top`

Scope: `write` · MCP: `slate_doc pin_to_top`

Pin a document (file, page or folder) to the top of its drawer or folder listing, for everyone. Pinned entries come first in `GET /lists/{id}/drawer`, oldest pin first.

- Returns: `200` [DocOut](#docout)

### `DELETE /docs/{doc_id}/top`

Scope: `write` · MCP: `slate_doc unpin_from_top`

Take a document off the top of its listing.

- Returns: `200` [DocOut](#docout)

### `GET /docs/{doc_id}/revisions`

Scope: `read` · MCP: `slate_doc revisions`

A file doc's revisions, newest first (metadata; the bytes are at each `url`).

- Returns: `200` [list of DocRevisionOut](#docrevisionout)

### `GET /docs/{doc_id}/revisions/compare`

Scope: `read` · MCP: `slate_doc compare_revisions`

What changed between two revisions of a file doc (`to` default: the current one), by type: text files line by line; CSV, TSV and XLSX cell by cell per sheet; PDFs by their extracted text (approximate); images and the rest have no server diff.

- Query: `from`\*, `to`
- Returns: `200` [CompareOut](#compareout)

### `POST /docs/{doc_id}/revisions`

Scope: `write`

Upload the next revision of a file doc (raw body, up to 25 MB). The previous revision stays, marked superseded. `note` says what changed; it is required.

- Query: `filename`\*, `note`\*
- Body: `application/octet-stream`
- Returns: `201` [DocRevisionOut](#docrevisionout)

### `POST /docs/{doc_id}/revisions/base64`

Scope: `write` · MCP: `slate_doc upload`

The same upload for clients that can only send JSON.

- Body: `Base64RevisionIn`: `filename`\*, `content_base64`\*, `content_type`, `note`\*
- Returns: `201` [DocRevisionOut](#docrevisionout)

### `POST /docs/{doc_id}/revisions/{revision_no}/restore`

Scope: `write` · MCP: `slate_doc restore_revision`

Make an older revision current again, as a new revision with its bytes.

- Returns: `200` [DocOut](#docout)

### `POST /attachments/{attachment_id}/promote`

Scope: `write` · MCP: `slate_item promote_attachment`

Move a task's attachment into Docs & Files: a new file doc with the bytes as revision 1; the task loses the attachment and gets a comment linking the doc.

- Body: `PromoteIn`: `title`, `parent_id`, `list_id`, `section_id`, `note`
- Returns: `201` [DocOut](#docout)

### `GET /doc-files/{file_id}`

Scope: `read`

The file's bytes; images show inline unless `?download=true`.

- Query: `download`
- Returns: `200`

### `DELETE /doc-files/{file_id}`

Scope: `write` · MCP: `slate_doc remove_file`

Remove File

- Returns: `204`

### `GET /docs/{doc_id}/comments`

Scope: `read` · MCP: `slate_doc comments`

Every comment on the doc, oldest first; threads are the rows sharing a `parent_id`.

- Returns: `200` [list of DocCommentOut](#doccommentout)

### `POST /docs/{doc_id}/comments`

Scope: `write` · MCP: `slate_doc comment`

Comment on a page or file. With `anchor` it starts a review thread (a quoted span on a page; a page number and/or a spot on a file); without, it is discussion. `parent_id` replies in a thread. `suggestion_md` proposes replacement text for the quote (pages). `assignee` makes it an Ask. `@handle` mentions and the Ask reach the inbox and webhooks.

- Body: `DocCommentIn`: `body_md`\*, `parent_id`, `viewed_revision`, `anchor`, `suggestion_md`, `assignee`
- Returns: `201` [DocCommentOut](#doccommentout)

### `GET /docs/{doc_id}/activity`

Scope: `read` · MCP: `slate_doc activity`

The side panel's feed: the doc's comments and the events folded in as activity lines.

- Query: `limit`
- Returns: `200` [DocActivityOut](#docactivityout)

### `PATCH /doc-comments/{comment_id}`

Scope: `write` · MCP: `slate_doc edit_comment`

Edit your own comment.

- Body: `DocCommentPatch`: `body_md`\*
- Returns: `200` [DocCommentOut](#doccommentout)

### `POST /doc-comments/{comment_id}/resolve`

Scope: `write` · MCP: `slate_doc resolve_comment`

Close a review thread or an Ask (the thread's first comment).

- Returns: `200` [DocCommentOut](#doccommentout)

### `POST /doc-comments/{comment_id}/reopen`

Scope: `write` · MCP: `slate_doc reopen_comment`

Reopen

- Returns: `200` [DocCommentOut](#doccommentout)

### `POST /doc-comments/{comment_id}/assign`

Scope: `write` · MCP: `slate_doc assign_comment`

Address the comment to an account (an Ask), or take it off (`assignee: null`).

- Body: `DocCommentAssignIn`: `assignee`
- Returns: `200` [DocCommentOut](#doccommentout)

### `POST /doc-comments/{comment_id}/accept`

Scope: `write` · MCP: `slate_doc accept_suggestion`

Apply a review comment's suggestion to the page (an ordinary save, so page history has it) and resolve the thread.

- Returns: `200` [AcceptOut](#acceptout)

## workload

### `GET /workload/boxes`

Scope: `read` · MCP: `slate_workload boxes`

The Box view's numbers: per person and agent, plus one box for unassigned tasks, open and in-progress counts, overdue, finished in the last `done_days` days, and open load against this week's capacity.

- Query: `kinds`, `section_id`, `list_id`, `done_days`
- Returns: `200` [BoxesOut](#boxesout)

### `GET /capacities`

Scope: `read` · MCP: `slate_workload capacities`

Every person's and agent's capacity, defaults included.

- Query: `kinds`
- Returns: `200` [list of CapacityOut](#capacityout)

### `GET /accounts/{account_id}/capacity`

Scope: `read` · MCP: `slate_workload capacity`

Get Capacity

- Returns: `200` [CapacityOut](#capacityout)

### `PATCH /accounts/{account_id}/capacity`

Scope: `write` · MCP: `slate_workload set_capacity`

Set an account's capacity: your own, or anyone's as an owner or admin.

- Body: `CapacityIn`: `hours_per_day`, `tasks_per_day`, `work_days`
- Returns: `200` [CapacityOut](#capacityout)

### `DELETE /accounts/{account_id}/capacity`

Scope: `write` · MCP: `slate_workload reset_capacity`

Back to the defaults for the account's kind.

- Returns: `200` [CapacityOut](#capacityout)

## data

### `GET /export`

Scope: `read` · MCP: `slate_export json`

Download a list (`list_id`), a section (`section_id`) or everything. JSON holds every task with its comments, checklists, time and links, docs pages, the scope's chat channels (messages, thread replies, reactions), plus the structure around them; CSV is one row per task for a spreadsheet. Trashed tasks are never included.

- Query: `format`, `list_id`, `section_id`, `include_archived`
- Returns: `200`

### `GET /admin/backup`

Scope: `admin`

A consistent copy of the whole database (SQLite), taken while Slate keeps running. Holds everything, token fingerprints and encrypted secrets included: admins only.

- Returns: `200`

### `POST /trash/empty`

Scope: `admin` · MCP: `slate_export empty_trash`

Delete everything in the trash for good (admins). History stays.

- Returns: `200` [EmptiedOut](#emptiedout)

## health

### `GET /health`

Scope: `read` · MCP: `slate_health get`

Slate's health, for owners and admins: `status` (ok, warn or fail: the worst of `checks`), each background poller (reminders, digest, due nudges, recurring, trash) with its last run, last success, error and failures in a row, the engines (scheduler, webhooks, automations, push), calls per token over the last hour (errors, error rate, slow calls, average and worst time) with recent examples, request latency percentiles, failed automation runs in the last day, queue depths and engine lag, and database size and free disk. Counters start over when Slate restarts. A poller that fails `alert_after` runs in a row records `health.alert` (and `health.recovered` once it works again).

- Returns: `200` [HealthOut](#healthout)

## search

### `GET /search`

Scope: `read` · MCP: `slate_search search`

Find `q` in task titles and descriptions, doc titles, page text and the text inside files, and chat messages, in one call. Tasks come first, then docs, then messages, each group sharing `limit` (default 30). Only what you can read; `%` and `_` are literal.

- Query: `q`\*, `limit`
- Returns: `200` [SearchOut](#searchout)

## settings

### `GET /settings/agents`

Scope: `admin` · MCP: `slate_account agent_rules`

What agent accounts may never do in this workspace, whatever their token or role. With nothing saved, agents may not delete for good, archive sections or lists, share, or issue tokens. People, owners and admins included, are never limited by this.

- Returns: `200` [AgentRulesOut](#agentrulesout)

### `PUT /settings/agents`

Scope: `admin` · MCP: `slate_account set_agent_rules`

Replace what agent accounts may never do (`denied`, a list of action keys). Owner or admin people only: an agent may not change this, even on an admin token. Recorded as a `settings.changed` event.

- Body: `AgentRulesIn`: `denied`\*
- Returns: `200` [AgentRulesOut](#agentrulesout)

## events

### `GET /events`

Scope: `read` · MCP: `slate_events poll`

Events after `since`, oldest first. The polling fallback for agents without a doorbell. `actor` (handle or id) keeps one account's events: a per-agent audit trail. `tail=true` returns the newest `limit` (what just happened), still oldest first.

- Query: `since`, `type`, `item_id`, `actor`, `actor_kind`, `tail`, `limit`
- Returns: `200` [EventPage](#eventpage)

### `POST /events/{event_id}/revert`

Scope: `write` · MCP: `slate_item revert`

Undo one recorded item change by issuing its inverse as you: an `item.updated` on a field (title, priority, dates, waiting on, description, tags...), `item.status_changed`, `item.assigned` or `item.moved`. The log is append-only, so this writes a new event (its `session_ref` is `revert:<event id>`) through the same access checks as a PATCH. 409 when the field has changed again since that event (nothing is written); 422 for any other event type.

- Returns: `200` [ItemOut](#itemout)

### `GET /events/stream`

Scope: `read`

Live events as SSE (`id` = event id, `event` = type, `data` = payload JSON).

- Query: `since`, `type`, `item_id`, `actor`, `token`
- Returns: `200`

## recurrences

### `GET /recurrences`

Scope: `read` · MCP: `slate_recurrence list`

List Recurrences

- Query: `list_id`, `include_ended`
- Returns: `200` [list of RecurrenceOut](#recurrenceout)

### `GET /recurrences/preview`

Scope: `read` · MCP: `slate_recurrence preview`

Try a rule without saving it: the next `count` occurrences and the rule in plain words. With `trigger=on_done` the dates assume each one is done on its due day, starting today. A rule Slate would refuse is a 422 with the reason.

- Query: `rrule`\*, `dtstart`, `timezone`, `count`, `trigger`, `skip_weekends`
- Returns: `200` [PreviewOut](#previewout)

### `GET /recurrences/upcoming`

Scope: `read` · MCP: `slate_recurrence upcoming`

Dates scheduled rules will fill between `start` and `end` (YYYY-MM-DD, inclusive, at most 400 days) that are not items yet, for drawing future repeats on a calendar. Paused, ended and `on_done` rules have none.

- Query: `start`\*, `end`\*, `list_id`
- Returns: `200` [list of UpcomingOut](#upcomingout)

### `GET /recurrences/{rule_id}`

Scope: `read` · MCP: `slate_recurrence get`

Get Recurrence

- Returns: `200` [RecurrenceOut](#recurrenceout)

### `POST /recurrences`

Scope: `write` · MCP: `slate_recurrence create`

Create a rule. Instances appear on the next scheduler tick (within a minute), or at once with `POST /recurrences/{id}/run-now`.

- Body: `RecurrenceIn`: `body_template_md`, `priority`, `tags`, `assignees`, `dtstart`, `timezone`, `lead_days`, `missed_policy`, `trigger`, `skip_weekends`, `reopen`, `copy_checklists`, `list_id`\*, `title_template`\*, `rrule`\*, `adopt_item_id`
- Returns: `201` [RecurrenceOut](#recurrenceout)

### `PATCH /recurrences/{rule_id}`

Scope: `write` · MCP: `slate_recurrence update`

Update Recurrence

- Body: `RecurrencePatch`: `body_template_md`, `priority`, `tags`, `assignees`, `dtstart`, `timezone`, `lead_days`, `missed_policy`, `trigger`, `skip_weekends`, `reopen`, `copy_checklists`, `list_id`, `title_template`, `rrule`, `ended`
- Returns: `200` [RecurrenceOut](#recurrenceout)

### `POST /recurrences/{rule_id}/pause`

Scope: `write` · MCP: `slate_recurrence pause`

Pause Recurrence

- Returns: `200` [RecurrenceOut](#recurrenceout)

### `POST /recurrences/{rule_id}/resume`

Scope: `write` · MCP: `slate_recurrence resume`

Resume from today; occurrences that fell inside the pause are not spawned.

- Returns: `200` [RecurrenceOut](#recurrenceout)

### `POST /recurrences/{rule_id}/run-now`

Scope: `write` · MCP: `slate_recurrence run_now`

Materialize this rule now: everything due within its lead window, under its policy.

- Returns: `200` [RunNowOut](#runnowout)

### `POST /recurrences/{rule_id}/adopt`

Scope: `write` · MCP: `slate_recurrence adopt`

Make an existing item this rule's current occurrence. A dated item keeps its due date; an undated one takes the rule's next occurrence. The rule spawns from the one after.

- Body: `AdoptIn`: `item_id`\*
- Returns: `200` [ItemOut](#itemout)
